They do a lot.

But it's, it's very similar work in that it's immersive and design led and they're looking for more companies to acquire particularly in the US they have another company called Hovercraft.
Hovercraft Studio.
If you're, if you're doing a Google for them, they come up Hovercraft Studio, their domain.
I think I've heard of it.
Yeah, yeah, good, good.
Because that, that's, that means you're probably in the right space for us as well.
So, so yeah, essentially we're looking for, for more companies that are like that.
Definitely.
Hovercraft, we'll be looking for companies with.
I mean, I've got to say, just looking at your homepage and your website, it's very similar vibe to Hovercraft as well.
And basically, the guys at Hovercraft now, they're probably about half a year to a little bit longer, about half a year in.
And they're very much a part of the senior leadership of what the investment team are doing.
So they're getting excited looking at companies like yours and talking to founders like you, of which we haven't done a ton yet because we've only just kind of finished integrating them.
So we're now on the next phase where we're looking for more agencies to come in.
But very much Hovercraft are the sort of lead agency within the Skyview business.
And Skyview is our client, Skyview.
So I am, first of all, entertaining conversations like this because I think we're, as you all know, the industry is in a very interesting situation.
I am talking to a couple of folks as well.
One is a company called Merge.
They're in New York City.
And, you know, they work with smaller agencies, you know, acquiring.
And they've gave us.
They've given me, like, how the deal structure is.
It happens with them.
We engage with them, we pay them a fee.
They look for buyers.
They match us with folks.
The reason why I'm having this conversation is for a couple of personal reasons.
I think I've spent the last 15 years, 15, 18 years of my career building a company.
I do know that businesses are just like any other living entity.
You know, it has its beginning, its end.
And personally, I just feel like I could spend more time with my kid.
I run the business with my husband.
And it's just, we want to see our options.
I've had this health scare, so I'm dealing with some of that on the personal side.
So I'm really at this point of, like, how much further can I take this?
How can I be of use to others?
And, you know, so it's sort of that fork in the road for a founder.
Sorry, how can I make this bigger?
How can I.
Because that's my job is to make sure that this thing I created lives on.
I guess, philosophically, that's where I am in terms of.
I'm looking at the website, Hovercraft, definitely there's, you know, just visually, there's an alignment with that.
I am talking to other founders as well.
I'm curious about.
I'm in this group of other studios in New York City, I'm regularly having conversations with.
Also studio in Texas already been chewed, I think is the name some of the founders in New York City as well, versus I'm always having conversations with different studio owners.
Like, how do you see this?
How do you feel?
How do you feel like the, the way that the economic downturns are happening?
How are you navigating that?
So I'm keeping a lot of these options open for me as a founder.
Like, what can I do?
Do I, Do I.
How do I navigate this hard turn?
Luckily for us, it's been a bit better this year than last year.
Last year was, I felt like, was a really difficult year for us.
So, yeah, so for me, it's curiosity why I'm being pulled into these conversations because I want to know.
All right, well, let's.
Let's fill in the details.
So.
So these, these calls for us and why we're involved is, is basically we are looking for good targets for our client.
What we're not looking to do is find companies necessarily that are for sale.
Although it sounds like you're speaking to Merge and you've listed the company for sale on.
On their website.
Merge is a very similar company to Agencies Co.
Our website.
It's a very similar idea.
We both work in the agency space.
So you're obviously listing with those guys.
No, not yet.
I haven't listed with them yet, but I am having a conversation with them.
All right, okay, that makes sense.
And so our client is more focused on good matches than they are just finding companies that are for sale.
So that's why we're approaching you out of the blue, because we're.
We're not necessarily looking to find a company with problems.
We're looking for founders that want to stay in the business a certain amount of time because particularly for our client, they're building something with quite a big vision and they're hoping.
I don't know whether the involvement is with you now.
Are you looking to get out?
Is your partner still involved?
Yeah, we're 100% involved.
I think for us, we are curious just like, what's outside there?
Like, how can we.
What's the best ways to maximize what we've built?
Yeah.
Okay.
Well, this, this is going to be a great option because just generally speaking, I'm sure Merge have taken you through all the deal structures.
Very often you'll get a bit of money up front and then you get a certain period to work, and it's usually three years.
You can get, you know, shorter periods of time.
But what generally happens is the value of the business goes down with that.
You know, the briefer it is.
These guys are looking for founders that want to stay in a certain amount of time.

So certainly if your, your husband, your partner is involved with the business day to day and wants to stay in over the next three to five years, then there, there could be a, a good up sort of option for you guys because there's a lot of upside that's coming with this business.
So these guys have built and sold many cloud computing businesses before and they've worked with private equity before and they built businesses and sold them for a lot of money before.
And what they're seeing is a similar sort of progression in the way that people are using immersive and 3D and AR experiences to how the Internet started 30 years ago when they got into it.

And when they first started working, they were working at Microsoft and some other cloud computing companies and they built a lot of the early Internet companies with Microsoft that went on to earn tons of money.
So they're seeing some similarities and they're out the other side of that very much could be retired golf players, but they decided that this is the one last deal that they want to do and build.
And so there's a huge amount of upside for them because they, I mean, these guys are a players and they're used to, you know, selling into the enterprise at the top level.
So they're building a business that will be worth hundreds of millions, definitely 100 million minimum.

And so if you're, if you or your, your partner want to stay in this business, there's equity, roll over into the bigger holding company and there's a, there's a big opportunity as well as all of that, there's a huge creative opportunity as well, working alongside hovercraft.
I'm sure you can see I don't, you know, you said you heard of them, but I'm sure you can see these guys are at the peak of their game as well.
They're extremely good at what they do and they are also growing very, very fast at the moment.

So our job, yeah, is really to find, create companies like yours and then kind of see if you're up for it and get that next conversation arranged with our client so you can really find out what it is that they're pitching, what the big strategy is, and whether it's a fit for you personally as well.
So just on this call, what we're looking to do is have some details to go into that call with, with our clients.
So if you can sort of very generally give us a sort of quick back story of how the business was, was built and also what it is that you guys are good at and what you focus on, those types of things.
That's so interesting because I, I have an interview, I have a podcast interview.
I'm actually preparing for these calls.
I do a podcast as well.
So I'm used to asking all this.
Fantastic, but not quite as you know, figured out.
But we started this business back in 2016, 2008.
We were freelancing back in the Philippines with my, with my husband.
My husband is from the city, so he's, he was the guy who had like a plan.
And this is what happens in this industry in New York, in New York, in the west, like this is how it's run.
And I was coming from the Philippines and we, we, we started our small studio there.
So until today I still, I still run a studio in the Philippines.
So I'm very adept at running a global, a global operation.
In fact, I'm doing an eor an employee of record with another with a different business helping them set up their talent pool in Manila.

That is one of my like secret, like non creative things I'm very good at is operating, running and operating different locales and like really understanding costing in different parts of the world and adherence and compliance which I didn't realize was a skill until I'm like selling it to other people.
And then in 2013 I got my green card.
So I did my great.
And then we started another studio here and we basically created another llc.
So we have a studio here right now.
We have about 10 staff in the Philippines and we have, we are just a group of four in New York.
But right now with our freelancers we're, we could scale up to 20.
Our biggest project was with Mega the Sally and creating some assets for a documentary film.
So we scaled up around 50 people at that point and everything is, we're all remote but just sort of understanding how that workflow process works out.
Something we've, you know, we keep working and fixing the last few years.
We, right now most of our, one of our biggest challenges is that we are whitelisted with another studio in New York City.
We work with one of our partners who was a former partner from Aardman called Nathan Love.
So a lot of our projects do come from them, which is a lot of it is in pharmaceuticals.
So we're very well versed in the world of pharma.
Animation, motion design.

But in the last few, the last two years we've been trying to work, really working directly with brands and one of the more exciting things we've done is working with this entity called American Documentary.
They are the production arm for PBS and we've done some brand strategy workshops with them.
And right now speaking of immersive, we are working with a musician and doing all their stage narrative design, sorry, animation narrative for their tour happening this summer.
His name is Kashmir.
And then we're in talks with, we have a really great partnership with this Hollywood director.
So we are in talks with making two more documentaries with her.
One is produced by RZA from the Wu Tang Clan and then the other one is going to be for a yet to be named.
I can't say all the details but it's for a documentary for an NBA player.
So we've got that partnership rolling along and then you know, we've got the commercial, we do pharmaceutical commercials for like the wpps, IPG Health, all of these big agencies.
So you're white label, they've got the client.
We are white labeled.
Yeah, yeah.
But yeah, so, so those are the mix of projects that we have.
And so those relationships with the agencies, why is it just pharmaceutical that they come to you for?
Is that.
How did that end up being your specialty?
So it was, you know, in the beginning of our, when we moved to the United States we weren't very savvy with our marketing and our sales.

So we were sort of like given that, you know, in this business you're known for your last project and sort of we started doing one character animation project and then that sort of given birth to more projects like that and it kind of just became a sort of reliable source of income for us creating these explainer videos for pharmaceutical brands, doing instruction for use or moas.
So that's just something that kind of happened and like we grew into it and that's sort of how that.
What's the, the fit with the, the sort of subculture and the emerging markets and that side of things, you know, culture, art.
Because that's very much the vibe that your website gives off as well.
Yes, yes.
So one of the things that we've been working on is for example the relationship with this director.
She's.
She's a queer bipoc and woman of color and the, and the, and the, what do you call it?
The, I guess the areas of interest where we work with her art, music, hip hop culture and stuff like that.
Like even the two upcoming projects that we have.
And that's something that we've.
In terms of marketing and really being intentional of what spaces we want to fill in, that's the direction.

And sort of the pharmaceutical is sort of the, I would say the capital backbone of how we grew our operations and sort of also finessed our skills, both technically, but in terms of where we want to take the brand.
It's really where culture lies.
And so you've got a cash cow with the pharmaceutical stuff and basically stylistically is more.
More in tune with the stuff that you've got there.
Yeah.
Okay, cool.
And then just in terms of your team, you did say that everybody's working remotely.
So the four that are based in the us are they all creative or is it management?
So it's.
We've got.
So the creatives are me and my husband and the rest both are.
One is a producer and one is an associate producer.
And then if we do need to get artists, we either source from Europe or Asia.
And then of course, our team in Manila.
And so the team in Manila is all creative and some admin.
So you've got like your manager and anyone, just because of the way that the structures there are.
It's.
You need to have a big team for compliance, for administrative compliance in the Philippines.
So that's what they do.
Okay, brilliant.
But obviously the price of running that staff is obviously minimal compared to having the same size team in New York, I should imagine.
Okay.
And then in terms of like, can you give me a ballpark?
I know we're not in NDA, but can you give me sort of ballpark figures?
You said you had a bad year last year.
Yes, I think you weren't the only one.
There's been a few things in the industry that's.
That's colluded against everybody, but if you can just give us some ballpark, you know, what was your revenue?
What was your revenue was around.
Sorry, let me have my QuickBooks here.
I think it was around.
If you can give me a list, I can.
I can send it to you.
But I think, let me see, it was around 600, 000.
That was a really low year for us.
What is it this year?
What do you think it's going to be this year?
I think we.
If all our projections are correct, we would hit around a million plus, like 1.1 to 1.4.
And that's like a.
Did you lose money last year?
Oh, yeah.
Oh, yeah.
What about this year?
You're going to be profitable again?
I think at the least it Will be break even.
Yeah.
All right.
And then in terms of, like, your.
Your sort of appetite to sell, obviously you're looking to sell at the moment.
What is it you're looking for?
Is it purely for your health reasons and for more time with your family, or is there anything else at play?
I think it's.
That's why we use the word curious.
Because what would be what I.
I think for me, it's just.
I would love to be.
I've, you know, as a founder, you.
You have all these skills, and how do I take it to the next level, I guess, is my one thing.
And then if I do believe in these skills, so great and so amazing, how can I do that?
That I only work a reasonable amount of time and spend more time with my kid and, you know, my family.
So that's really the thing.
How can I leverage my specialty?
So one of my challenges was because last year, it was a bad year, I had to take in all of these responsibilities that I could put on other people before.
And so now I feel like I'm doing a lot of the things I've graduated from.
But I just, you know, I have no, I had.
Just because.
Just because until, like, we.
We get into a good spot.
So.
So a part of me has no more appetite for, for example, like the basic things like revising something for the client.
Like, I used to have a lead for that, and I really don't want to do that, but it's just something that I have to do.
Like right now, Google is a client.
One of these note takers does all the work.
Exactly.
I know, exactly.
Like, you know, like, for example, Google is the client right now.
They keep coming back to us.
It's great.
Margins are small, but it's easy.
But it's also, like, I used to have one person I can just give that for, but now I have to do the revisions myself.
So it's all of these little frustrations that I feel like I really should be graduating from, taking the fun out of it.
So maybe this is an interesting route for you as well, because being part of a bigger organization will take some of that away from you, and certainly they can help fund it.
I think one of the things they're looking to do is find really great creatives like you guys are and give you more work.
They've got tons and tons of work that's coming through them.
They've.
They've almost doubled in size since they.
They got the investment from our client.
So certainly they would be looking to share more work with you as well.
So there'd be a lot more coming through.
I've got to be completely honest.

They, they will, they will talk about this on the call, but because you haven't been profitable last year, because you're not profitable this year and I don't know what merges have said to you, but you know, valuations are based on how profitable the company is and it's a multiple of that that becomes profit.
But these guys are very good at these types of offers.
What they do is they, they can set something in the, in the future and they share all of the profits until we all get to that place.
So they are very good at absorbing smaller studios and helping them to become more profitable.
But it may mean that there won't be a big massive chunk of cash at the front because they just can't structure their deals like that with the people that give them the money to do the deals.
You know, the lenders won't structure it.
So I'm not, that's not to say that there won't be any kind of cash at all at the front, but just they, I'm just warning you not, it's not going to be.
This transaction wouldn't be the one that's going to be life changing apart from you guys will be able to step back and take the stress out of it.
But they are building towards something where everybody exits free for a bigger amount of money and you would be part of that.
So it's, it's kind of what are you looking to trade?
You know, you said about the stress levels and being able to spend more time with your family.
Well, certainly this would give you that, but it may not give you that life changing amount of cash.

But anyway, I just want to be upfront with you because we've been through this process a few times with agencies that haven't broken even for a few years and you know, I don't want to throw any surprises your way.
I appreciate it, but it's not a billion dollars.
No, I think I'm very realistic when it comes to that.
I understand how.
Yeah, it's not, this is not like finally my wishes have come true.
Well then some of the wishes will be, some of the wishes will be becoming true, but just maybe not that one with the bank balance just yet.

But they're very, their offers are very generous with the founders so that they can go full, you know, go forward as part of the management team and then earn that money as the reward in the, in the future rather than like on the day, so.
But anyway, look, does this sound like something you'd be interested in, catching up with these guys on the next call?
Okay, brilliant.
So the next steps for us is we have a weekly meeting with our client, and obviously we.
We give them an update on everybody that we've spoken to.
So they know that you were on our list for our meeting last week.
So we'll give them an update, and if they're happy to move forward as well, we'll let let you know.
But it's good to know that you're willing to make yourself available for that call.
Yes.
Okay.
Fabulous.
All right, well, thank you very much for your time.
I really appreciate that.
Same.
Likewise.
Have a great day.
We'll speak soon.
You, too.
All right.
Bye.
Bye.
So much.

summary.overview: The M&A Exploration Meeting between Rezonate.tv and Capital A centered on potential acquisition strategies for Rezonate.tv, as Katwo Librando discussed her motivations for exploring M&A options, including a desire for personal time and industry insights. Andrew from Capital A outlined their role as M&A advisors for marketing services companies, emphasizing the importance of matching founders who are willing to remain in their businesses post-acquisition. The meeting reviewed Rezonate.tv's history as a creative studio founded in 2008, its current operations spanning the Philippines and New York, and its evolving focus towards cultural collaborations while maintaining financial stability through pharmaceutical projects. Future revenue projections were discussed, alongside the recognition that recent profitability issues could influence valuation. The conversation concluded with an agreement for Andrew to present Rezonate.tv to his client, with Katwo open to future discussions regarding the acquisition.
